stories.extract: The Boston Braves were a Major League Baseball team that played in Boston for the National League from 1871 to 1952. The team relocated to Milwaukee after the 1952 season, becoming the Milwaukee Braves, and subsequently moved to Atlanta in 1966.

stories.text: The Troy Trojans complain that new "reserve system" has already been violated with the Chicago White Stockings signing of Troy pitcher Fred Goldsmith.
stories.headline: Troy Complains Chicago Signs Pitcher Fred Goldsmith

image.alt: Engraved portrait of a mustached man with ornate frame, 1886 newspaper

stories.extract: Fredrick Ernest Goldsmith was an American right-handed pitcher in 19th-century professional baseball in both the U.S. and Canada. In his prime, Goldsmith was six-foot-one-inch tall and weighed 195 pounds.

stories.text: The Buffalo Bisons of the International League defeat the National League champion Boston Red Caps behind the pitching of Pud Galvin. The victory over the Red Caps gives Galvin a win over each team in the NL. He finishes the 1878 season with a combined 10–5 record against the NL clubs. Buffalo will become a member of the National League in 1879.
stories.headline: Galvin's Buffalo Bisons Defeat National League Champion Red Caps
